candidates.name: David Somers
Anil Singh
candidates.statement_to_voters:
Anil is proud to live in the friendly neighbourhood Lower Penn, close to the wonderful Wombourne village. He passionately beilieves local businesses should take priority for contracts with the local Council.

With very high levels of council tax, huge savings cound be generated by using systems thinking approaches by bringing the pothole fixing team in-house, devolving it to our District Council would create a more responsive service and end the cycle of botched repairs.

His highest priority is to promote 'good neightbours' across the District. Let's plant more trees, this will absorb carbon and enable nature to thrive.

candidates.name: Tracey Bailey
candidates.statement_to_voters:
Following the sad passing of Cllr Shanika Mahendran, I have been selected as the Labour Party candidate for the New Bradwell Ward in the by election which will take place on Thursday 24th September.

As an introduction, I have spent most of my life in Milton Keynes, growing up nearby in Great Linford. I’ve recently taken early retirement but spent most of my working life at Cranfield University. I’ve been a governor at two primary schools, and I have previously served as a City Councillor, working with Shanika and Stephen Brown, who holds the other seat in the ward.

I’m currently getting to know the area better. I’ve already been out delivering leaflets which you may have seen, and I will be starting to knock on doors and introduce myself in person in the next few days.

I’ve already got experience of helping people with issues such as road safety, fly tipping, and surface water flooding, and will be keen to find out what matters to people in this area.

I’ve heard that anti-social behaviour and theft from cars is an issue in some places, so I’ve spoken to Chris Curtis MP to see if we can arrange a meeting with Thames Valley Police to see how councillors can assist neighbourhood officers in investigating and addressing these problems.

candidates.name: Julian Vernon Camies
candidates.statement_to_voters: I have lived in Milton Keynes for nearly 40 years. I understand the issues affecting residents. An engineer by trade, now retired, Im standing to represent you, root out waste and fund services important to you. New Bradwell needs Reform UK and together we can make the necessary changes.

candidates.name: John Joseph Baldwin
candidates.statement_to_voters:
John has been a dedicated campaigner for Riverside residents for many years. Many of you will remember his work to help save Deerswood Meadow from residential development, including gathering signatures and organising community email campaigns during the frosty February of 2022.

He has consistently scrutinised council decisions and pushed for stronger, fairer planning procedures — work he intends to continue. Riverside residents deserve experienced, independent voices who will act on the issues that matter most.

John looks forward to meeting as many of you as possible in the months ahead and to working for you, and only you, as your local councillor.

candidates.name: Nigel William Smith
candidates.statement_to_voters: ​A surveyor working in the telecommunications industry. He has lived in Maidenhead for nearly thirty years and is a school governor of a local primary school and was a former West London councillor.

candidates.name: Tom Bradley
candidates.statement_to_voters: Living in the heart of the division, I’m proud to be standing to be Campden Vale’s councillor. I will always champion our local area, making sure it gets its fair share of resource. I will protect our rural way of life – backing our farmers. And, I will secure extra investment for our local roads.

candidates.name: Bob Eastoe
candidates.statement_to_voters:
“A little about me.
I spent a career in industry with both start-up businesses and multi-nationals. I recently retired as Chief Operating Officer and Chief financial officer of one of Buckinghamshire’s largest manufacturers and private employers. Over the 13 years I was with them we became:
 - the first business of its kind in the world to be carbon neutral over 10 years ago, 
- the first of its kind to achieve ISO Environmental Management accreditation,
- the first business of its kind to use British Red Tractor wool in our product and won a Queen’s Award for Sustainability in 2020. 
During this time, the business more than tripled its turnover and improved its profitability demonstrating that good environmental practice is good business practice.
 
I moved to Moreton-in-Marsh in March 2022 with my wife after having lived in our last village for 32 years where we brought up our three children. It is now time for me to spend my time and expertise supporting those less fortunate than myself and serve our community. I am a volunteer driver for Cotswold friends and I am privileged to have represented the people of Moreton as a town councillor since September 2022.
 
I stood to represent the people, businesses and environment of the new South Cotswolds constituency in the 2024 General Election to ensure meaningful progress on the Climate and Ecology Emergency is taken and that we build a fair and thriving future for us all.
 
I am now standing in the forthcoming Cotswold District Council election for The Rissington's ward so that the excellent work done by Green Councillor Andrew McLean can be continued. Local democracy will be a big part of the agenda in these elections and I shall ensure peoples' voices are heard about decisions that affect them in the transition to a new unitary authority and how they can continue to be heard in an ever-centralising political landscape.
 
I am a founder of "Moreton Against Over Development" as I am concerned about the potentially devastating effects this will have on the North Cotswolds, Stow and The Rissingtons.

candidates.name: Matt Fincham
candidates.statement_to_voters: Matt Fincham is a public relations consultant and small business owner, a British Army veteran and officer in the Army Reserve. He has lived in the Cotswolds for five years, having grown up in Churchdown, near Gloucester. Matt comes from a farming family and is a strong supporter of farming, countryside industries and the traditional rural way of life. With his rural roots, Matt understands how the needs of people across the Cotswolds differ from cities and aims to champion the views of and issues of Blockley residents and scrutinise council plans to ensure the best outcomes for our area of the Cotswolds.

candidates.name: Danny Loveridge
candidates.statement_to_voters:
I've lived in the North Cotswolds for nearly all of my life. It’s my home. I attended St Catherine's Primary School Chipping Campden School, and I've worked in the private sector, for charities and in the public sector.
Whenever I've thought about moving away from the area, there have always been things that pull me back: our beautiful countryside, our fantastic local pubs and independent businesses, but most of all, the people.
During this campaign, you'll hear a lot from other parties about easy fixes and simple solutions. I'm not going to promise those, because I'm tired of politicians pretending they can snap their fingers and fix issues overnight.
What I will promise is to listen carefully, look at the evidence, and give the issues that matter to our community the sensible and measured response they deserve. Whatever decision is ultimately reached, I want it to reflect our community rather than being an easy short term political fix.
This by-election is about who is best placed to serve Blockley and bring people together. I have a plan for our area, whereas Reform want to push their national agenda locally.
• Save our hospital services - As your local district councillor, I will use my position to make standing up for services at North Cotswolds Hospital my number one priority.
• Supporting residents with the cost of living - Many people are feeling the pinch and I will work with officers at the Council to support residents and signpost them to help.
• Hold Thames Water to account.
I hope to meet you on the doorstep over the next few weeks, in the meantime please don’t hesitate to get in touch if you’d like to talk.

candidates.name: Rudi Dikty-Daudiyan
candidates.statement_to_voters:
Brighton and Hove Liberal Democrats are pleased to introduce Rüdi Dikty-Daudiyan as their candidate in the upcoming Queen’s Park by-election.  Rüdi is a freelance translator who is proud to have made his home in the Queen’s Park ward.

Rüdi says, “I couldn’t be happier to have made Brighton my home, but like many of our residents, I’m concerned about how it’s being run.  The current Labour council has a massive majority, and yet, we’re not seeing the results we deserve.  This is the sixth expensive by-election being held since they came into office.  That’s money that could have been spent on improving pavements, dealing with bins and recycling and anti-social behaviour.  If elected, I would focus on getting the basics right.

In his spare time, Rüdi plays for the Queen’s Park Tennis Club and volunteers for the Pug Dog Welfare & Rescue Association.  He lives in the ward with his husband and dog Emma.

candidates.name: Steve Gladwin
candidates.statement_to_voters:
Behind the grand facades around Queen’s Park itself are communities facing some of the worst relative poverty in the city.

That is being felt particularly hard by pensioners and families struggling to pay their bills.

I want to be a councillor who is visible, accessible and focused on the issues that make a real difference to people’s lives.

Mr Gladwin, who retired from the NHS earlier this summer, has pledged to put tackling the cost of living, pensioner poverty, and fuel poverty at the heart of his campaign.

He has also highlighted economic regeneration and support for the wider Brighton and Hove economy as key priorities, drawing on previous experience running a small business.

Mr Gladwin lives in the area and has worked in the NHS for nearly 30 years, including as an executive director at several trusts.

He also has experience in local government and worked as a journalist in Brighton and Hove, serving as political editor for a local newspaper.

candidates.name: Stefan Sönke Speckesser
candidates.statement_to_voters:
I want to bring Queen’s Park back to life and make sure Craven Vale gets the regular care, repairs and clean streets residents deserve.

I want to be an active local voice who follows up with the council to get the basics right and to deliver for our community: affordable housing for families, protecting our green spaces and improving schools and services for young people so families have absolute confidence in their children’s education and wellbeing.

candidates.name: Mark Strong
candidates.statement_to_voters:
“I’m honoured to stand alongside Clare and am looking forward to working with her in support of all the ward. I’ve seen firsthand how important it is to work with local people and groups to explain decisions and hopefully get agreement on important issues. I want to support the ties between the council and the hard work done by the many charities and voluntary groups in Brighton & Hove.

“As a transport planner who has worked for many councils across the UK, I’m keen to see a continuation of the current Green administration’s work on improving active and inclusive travel, especially walking and wheeling as well as cycling.”

candidates.name: Warren Ladyman
candidates.statement_to_voters: Warren Ladyman grew up in Amble. His mother and sister lives here too. He knew and was friends with the previous incumbent, Arty Hume, whose sad passing triggered this by-election. Warren is in tune with local issues, particularly the lack of infrastructure, despite all the new homes being built. He is determined to fight for his constituents for improved GP services to allow patients to be seen locally instead of Hadston or elsewhere. When elected, Warren will join the fight to save money in County Hall through local government efficiencies. Vote for change, vote for Warren, vote Reform 🇬🇧 🗳

candidates.name: Amy Spriggs
candidates.statement_to_voters:
Amble and the surrounding area mean so much to me. This is the area I love, where I’ve grown up, gone to school, worked and lived all my life. To now have the opportunity to put myself forward to represent the community I call home is something I’m incredibly proud of.

If I’m fortunate enough to be elected, I want to bring a positive, hardworking and constructive approach to the role — listening to local people, getting things done and always putting our communities first.

I also want to build a strong working relationship with councillors in neighbouring wards. Our communities are closely connected, and I believe we achieve far more when we work together as a team rather than allowing ward boundaries to get in the way.

I can’t thank Scott Dickinson enough for his encouragement, support and advice to this point. Having worked alongside Scott over the last five years, I’ve seen first-hand just how much can be achieved through hard work, determination and strong community relationships.

I’m excited for the weeks ahead, to get out there, speak to residents and listen to what matters to you.

Amble is my home. I’m proud of where I come from, and I’d be incredibly proud to have the opportunity to represent it.

candidates.name: Dave Buchanan
candidates.statement_to_voters:
-Strong local vocal candidate
-Passionate about Caithness
-Accountable, transparent and accessible
-Truly independent, no party to pander to, no political alliances
-Doing what is right, for locals in Wick & East Caithness

candidates.name: Mark Butcher
candidates.statement_to_voters:
Blackpool South is an opportunity for the constituents of Blackpool South constituency to send the strongest message to Westminster that they want change, they want traditional values, they want lower taxes, economic growth and opportunity for all, not just for multinational business. People want border control, economic competence, fairness, real equality, not artificial DEI targets, quotas and positive discrimination.

On the 4th of July, in Blackpool South, vote for Mark Butcher, vote Reform UK.

Mark Butcher, founder of Christian soup kitchen, Amazing Graze has been announced as the Reform UK prospective parliamentary candidate for the Blackpool South Constituency by election to be held on July 4th 2024.

candidates.name: Katie Helen Donnelli-Hunn
candidates.statement_to_voters:
This summer, Claremont lost a dedicated public servant, Councillor Ivan Taylor, who served local people for over 50 years.

As Claremont looks to the future, I believe residents deserve a councillor who will continue to put local people first.

I was born and raised in Blackpool, and this town has shaped so much of who I am. We have so much to be proud of and I believe there is something special about Claremont.
 
Claremont itself has been part of my life for as long as I can remember. I came here for workshops at Blackpool Central Library as a child, attended my first Blackpool Youth Council event here, recorded music at Rock Hard Studios, and have spent more family nights than I can count at Funny Girls. They might seem like small things, but they’re the memories that make somewhere feel like home and they’re part of why standing to represent Claremont feels so personal to me.

One of my core values is I feel passionately about people being heard, treated fairly, and supported when they need it. It’s what led me to study Law, to volunteer in legal advice centres helping people who couldn’t afford legal support, and ultimately to the work I do today.

I now work as a caseworker, helping people who are often dealing with some of the most difficult moments in their lives. That can mean working with councils, housing providers and public services, navigating systems that can feel impossible to navigate alone, or simply making sure somebody’s voice isn’t ignored.

And that work has taught me what good representation really looks like.
It’s about listening properly, taking people seriously, showing up and sticking with an issue until you’ve done everything you can to get something changed.

That’s the kind of councillor I want to be for Claremont.

candidates.name: Rob Jones
candidates.statement_to_voters:
*Claremont Deserves Better*

Too long have we have not been listened to with our concerns. We deserve the opportunity to be proud of our area but at this moment the council have not been interested in helping. There is litter everywhere, dirty alleys and dog poo. For myself and a lot of residents we have to dodge this mess every time we leave the front door of our homes.

I want to see a cleaner Claremont, we need our Parks to be clean and safe.

As someone who grew up in Claremont and still lives here, I feel what the rest of us feel on a day to day basis.

*Mental Health* is another important topic to me, I think organising more social events in the community, clubs and projects.

*The Cost of Living* we all are feeling the pinch of it. I would like to work on assisting the cost of living for Claremont.

As your councillor, I will be the first to hold up my hands and state I’m not infallible, I won’t always know the answer immediately but what I can promise is that I will go out of my way to learn, research and come up with my own answer. I will be your representative, I will listen to you and always fight your corner.

candidates.name: Robert Davies
candidates.statement_to_voters: Rob has been a Councillor since 2007 and living in the ward means that he knows firsthand just how disruptive the two bridge failures have been. He also aware of how bad the roads are in this rural ward. As an Independent candidate his only loyalty is to his constituents and therefore can put their interests first rather than that of a political party that has its own agenda.  Rural wards have not had a meaningful representation on Council committees in the past and, if re-elected, Rob will work hard to make sure that the Council is fully aware of rural issues. He undertakes to work in full collaboration with all Councillors to ensure the best outcome for Forth & Endrick. In the short-term that means getting the bridges repaired and, in the longer-term, doing everything possible to promote economic development in the Ward through better infrastructure.

candidates.name: Calvin Clark
candidates.statement_to_voters:
I’m Calvin Clark, and I’m standing as a candidate for Hirst Division because I want to see strong, reliable and accountable representation for our community.

If elected, my priorities would be:

* Keep our Park Run — supporting this valuable community activity and helping ensure it can continue.
* Clean and safe streets — tackling litter, fly-tipping and anti-social behaviour and pressing the council to keep our streets maintained.
* Care in the community — supporting vulnerable residents and making sure people in Hirst can access the help they need.
* Better neighbourhoods — championing parks, play areas and community spaces and working for improvements where residents identify problems.
* Help local businesses — supporting our high streets and local businesses and recognising the contribution they make to Hirst.
* Always listen — making myself available to residents and taking their concerns seriously.
* Speak up for residents — challenging decisions at County Council when they don’t work for Hirst.
* Be visible and proactive — getting out into the community, listening to people directly and following issues through.
* Reliable and accountable representation — keeping residents informed about what I am doing on their behalf and being answerable for my work at the council.

For me, local politics should be about the practical issues that affect people every day: our streets, parks, neighbourhoods, businesses and the services people rely on. I want to make sure Hirst has representation that is present, engaged and focused on the community.

candidates.name: Kerry Davison
candidates.statement_to_voters:
I am absolutely delighted to formally announce that I am standing as your Reform UK candidate for the upcoming Northumberland County Council by-election in the Hirst Ward.

The Hirst isn’t just an election boundary to me. I was born right there on George Street. I am a proud miner’s daughter, my dad worked at Woodhorn and Ellington pits, and our family lived through the strike. In fact, I was born in the Hirst, my surname should be Hirst!

We have spent the last 15 months working hard on the ground to bring active, visible representation back to our community.

We made history in May 2025 by breaking the traditional Labour monopoly on Ashington Town Council for the first time. As your Central Ward Town Councillor, I have spent the last year working on the frontline for our town across our key decision-making bodies. I sit actively on our Finance and General Services Committee, the Personnel Committee, and the Partnership Board. I am also a representative on the CCTV Group, the Youth Coordination Group, the Allotment Liaison Group, the Ashington Town Forum, and the NALC County Committee. I haven’t just talked about change; We have been delivering it.

Now, I am ready to take that exact same work ethic to County Hall to fight for the Hirst. For too long, our ward has suffered from a complete lack of engagement from its previous representative, who failed to attend a single council meeting for six consecutive months.

While the media and Labour try to play political blame games, the facts are simple: the moment he failed to perform his duties, he was booted out of Reform UK for good reason. We don’t protect inactivity; we demand results.

Our community faces real, urgent infrastructure pressures. I am fully focused on ensuring that the ongoing Hirst Master Plan and regional regeneration programmes deliver actual, tangible results for our neighbourhood rather than just promises on paper.
 
A staggering 83% of all licensed Houses in Multiple Occupation in Northumberland are crammed strictly into Ashington and Blyth, saturating the Hirst and Central wards. Our local youngsters and disabled residents are being completely ignored on housing waiting lists, and we must secure the necessary funding and support to look after our own local people.

At the same time, our vital public services are collapsing. Local residents cannot get an NHS dentist appointment or even a routine appointment with a GP, while our frontline infrastructure is left to deteriorate. I am standing to deliver results from these ongoing schemes and enforce a common-sense policy of local houses for local people, alongside real investment in our healthcare and public spaces.

This campaign isn’t starting on election day—we are already out there doing the work. 
Over the next month, our campaign teams will be thick on the ground across every single street in the Hirst. The turquoise wave is coming in again, and we are ready to fight for you.

But having your support on the doorsteps and on social media is only the first step. To deliver real, lasting change, we need every single resident to turn that support into action. We need you to actually get out and make your voice heard at the ballot box when polling day arrives on Thursday, 1st October 2026.

candidates.name: Edward Hudson Oakenfull
candidates.statement_to_voters:
Born in Derby. I am aged 56 years of age and have lived most of my life in Belper and Duffield where attended Ecclesbourne school for my A levels, now living on a farm in Denby.

My early career was as an estate agent working in the local area. The past 15 years I have been self employed as a property developer and investor.

I am passionate about sports and keeping fit, my main sport is tennis where I reached 47 in the seniors over 45's world rankings and captained England in the Seniors Four Nations competition. Until recently I was a council member for tennis main governing body, STGB. I love walking the amazing trails and footpaths we have in the beautiful Derbyshire Dales.

I have been despairing at how our country has been run for decades and for the love of my community and country decided that I needed to make a stand and will be trying all I can to be elected to represent and improve the lives of all the people in my constituency.

candidates.name: Bess Saunders
candidates.statement_to_voters:
After decades working in the NHS, Bess has seen first-hand the pressure on our public services. Now she’s ready to stand up for our local communities and make sure residents’ voices are heard.

Bess has been knocking on doors and talking to residents across Kilburn, Denby, Holbrook and Horsley to find out what matters most to residents.

One message has come through loud and clear: people are deeply concerned about development on our countryside — particularly the impact of solar farms, new electricity pylons and housing developments.

🌱 Bess will make sure local people have a strong voice on these issues.
This by-election is your chance to choose a councillor who will listen, speak up and stand up for our communities.

💚 Vote Green on October 8th

candidates.name: Juliette Nicola Stevens
candidates.statement_to_voters:
I am honoured and proud to have been selected by Reform UK to stand in the Amber Valley Borough Council by‑election for the Kilburn, Denby, Holbrook and Horsley ward on 8 October 2026, following the resignation of the previous Conservative Party councillor.

I am Interim Chair of Reform UK Amber Valley Branch, and a serving councillor at Denby Parish Council. With many years of experience fighting for people as a Town, Borough and County Councillor, I really hope that people will support me.  I am a farmer and am very active in the community fighting to stop the loss of our agricultural land due to solar farms and housing on the green belt.

I've been campaigning and running drop in sessions to help people to fight against the enormous pylons which threaten our beautiful Amber Valley, and am campaigning for the National Grid to put the supply off shore or underground instead, or along the M1 motorway.

Please support me so I can help protect and improve Kilburn, Denby, Holbrook and Horsley by being a voice for you at Amber Valley Borough Council.

candidates.name: Sagal Abdi-Wali
candidates.statement_to_voters:
I am delighted that local members have put their trust in me to be Labour’s candidate in the area I’ve grown up in.

This place welcomed my family as refugees and gave us hope when we needed it most. I am so grateful to have had the opportunity to build a life here, serving our community as a councillor, school governor, and community activist. Now I am standing to say thank you and to give back the hope you gave me.

Throughout this campaign, I promise to put our communities at the heart of everything I do, now and for the future. Together, we can make hope win.

candidates.name: Barmy Brunch
candidates.party_name_on_ballot: The Official Monster Raving Loony Party
candidates.statement_to_voters:
It's time to get Rid of the Bad Eggs & Political Hams

No Time for Breakfast - No Time for Lunch

VOTE BARMY BRUNCH For a Healthy Body & Mind

candidates.name: Ewan Cameron
candidates.statement_to_voters:
"I am honoured to have been selected as the Conservative Candidate for Holborn and St Pancras. This is the community where I have lived, raised my family, and call home.

From Georgian terraces, squares and the Regent's Canal to the Knowledge Quarter's research, AI and science organisations today, Holborn and St Pancras have enormous potential that, with the right political leadership, can become an even better place to live, work and belong. We need a Member of Parliament focused on safer streets, more family homes and cutting the cost of living.

While families are leaving Holborn & St Pancras, the Green leader wants to talk about Gaza. Holborn & St Pancras has recently endured a 'Never Here MP'. We do not want another one!

Under Kemi Badenoch's leadership, the Conservative Party has changed; we have clear, fully costed plans to recruit 10,000 more police officers, scrap stamp duty on family homes and cut bills with our Cheap Power Plan.

That is the message I look forward to campaigning on over the next coming weeks.”

candidates.name: Clare Fischer
candidates.statement_to_voters:
I have recently joined the CLIMATE PARTY , whose leader is ED GEMMELL .

In particular, the Climate Party is highly motivated to field a candidate for the upcoming Holborn & St Pancras by-election (the seat from which Keir Starmer recently resigned).  It would generate a lot of publicity and give them a platform to debate with and challenge the other parties.

Now, do not LAUGH, but, um – [blush] – I am to be that very candidate… as no-one else is available to do it.

Do not fear for my sanity.  I am only a ‘paper candidate’ as I’m too busy to do anything on this other than have my name on the ballot.  Others will do all the clever stuff.   I will not take part in any of the hustings, indeed not even go to the vote count as Alistair McGowan will be performing at Red Hedgehog on 8 October, when voting takes place. (Of course, either Labour or the Greens will win this seat in any case.)

candidates.name: George Galloway
candidates.statement_to_voters:
Our party will offer voters something different. We believe the political focus should be centred on wages, housing, energy, peace, public services and national renewal. Currently no other candidate offers the voters this choice.

The Greens with their support for the assisted dying Bill, and reckless backing for the war in Ukraine just this last week have shown voters they cannot be trusted to make choices that reflect the views of the majority of Britons. They are no alternative.

At a time when millions are struggling to heat their homes, pay their rent and provide for their families, we believe politics must focus on bread-and-butter issues and the economic wellbeing of ordinary people. Greens and Labour support sending endless £billions to Ukraine. Instead of addressing poverty, immigration, energy prices, they were voting together last week to introduce legislation to make killing people legal. We believe voters will welcome the chance to reject this madness.

We believe Britain's future lies in reindustrialisation, national sovereignty and economic policies that put workers, communities and productive industry first. For these reasons, we believe voters deserve a genuine socialist alternative, not simply another variation of the existing political consensus.

candidates.name: Tyler Kurtis Johnson
candidates.statement_to_voters:
Tyler is a lawyer who has called London home for the past ten years, living across the capital from north to west. Alongside his legal career he has served as a school governor, volunteered in schools providing careers advice, and mentored aspiring young lawyers who do not always have the connections to break into the profession.

He is an active member of his local community and attends church in the city, where he says he tries to live by the same values he wants to bring to public life, honesty, service and standing up for what is right.

We are being honest with the voters about this election.

Entirely because of mass immigration, this is not a seat a party promising deportations of any kind can win.

That’s just the electoral reality. For now, at least.

So for the remaining patriots in Holborn & St Pancras, this is a free hit.

An opportunity to send a message, the most powerful message, that you want your capital city back.

London is lost. It must be restored.

There is still time, just.

If you agree, then vote for it.

Vote Restore Britain.

candidates.name: Briony Anne Lonbay Kapoor
candidates.statement_to_voters:
I’m standing in the Holborn & St Pancras by-election on behalf of the Rejoin EU Party to give voice to the majority in favour of our membership of the EU and to protest that the main parties aren’t giving the issue the importance it merits.

As a long-term resident of the area, I’m aware of local issues and, if elected, would look forward to working on those matters with our local council.

Our constituency is arguably the most exciting one in the country, inclusive, creative, enterprising, hard working and great fun.

We’re well positioned to lead in London, in the UK and significantly to have a role at the heart of the EU.

candidates.name: Peter Newman
candidates.statement_to_voters:
As a former police detective, it depresses me to see the state of crime and policing in our capital. Residents no longer feel safe and our police officers are struggling to cope. Police stations are closing left, right and centre, yet Labour don’t care and our Mayor continues to gaslight Londoners over their safety.

I’m standing to ensure that people in Holborn & St Pancras feel safe on their own streets again. They deserve more than the chaos of Labour and the divisive and contradictory politics of the Green Party. Only Reform UK can offer them hope and a fresh start

candidates.name: Ketankumar Pipaliya
candidates.party_description_on_ballot: UK VOICE safer and stronger UK

candidates.name: Zack Polanski
candidates.statement_to_voters:
I am proud and honoured to have been selected for a byelection in the constituency where I have lived and worked for much of the past 20 years.

I love this place and so do the people whose doors I’ve knocked on in recent days – but it can be even better. I know times are tough in Holborn and St Pancras. My story of constant moving around flats is such a common story for Londoners – and I know many people here are really struggling right now. I’ll fight to turn this around.

Greens are underdogs here but we have the momentum – and I know we can achieve a historic victory in one of Labour’s safest seats. We will fight a positive campaign on the issues we know people care about, and to put as much pressure as we can on Labour to lower bills, for much more affordable housing and rent controls, to reduce massive wealth inequality and to make sure Labour don’t back down on climate action by allowing more North Sea drilling.

If elected, I will fight every day, in this constituency and in the Houses of Parliament, for the things people care about. Against injustice and on the side of ordinary people, not big money and the powerful.

candidates.name: Jonathan Silberman
candidates.statement_to_voters:
Jonathan Silberman, 75, is the organiser of the Communist League's Central Committee. He writes for The Militant newsweekly and is the director of Pathfinder Books. As a shopfloor worker in manufacturing industries over decades, he has led and
organised solidarity for strikes over jobs, wages, and union rights.
In the UK and internationally, Jonathan joins efforts to defend Cuba’s socialist revolution, fight Jew-hatred, back immigrant rights and build the communist movement.

He says:
"What working people in Holborn and St. Pancras, the UK and globally face now is a march by rival capitalist powers to World War III alongside a mounting attack on our living standards and rights. Cuba's workers and farmers face an accelerated assault on their socialist revolution as Washington with the tacit support of London seeks to crush that example. 
"Jew hatred is on the rise. Labour, Conservative, Green, Reform, Restore UK – capitalist parties all – have no faith in the capacities of toiling human beings. The march to war can only be ended by working people ourselves taking political power away from the propertied war mongers with their “dog-eat-dog” moral values – just as working people did in Cuba in 1959. 
"The Communist League says fighting Jew-hatred and defending Israel's existence as a refuge for Jews – is decisive for the working class, as well as pushing back attacks on immigrants and advancing solidarity with workers struggles internationally. Only by building a revolutionary working-class party to lead millions to replace capitalist rule can we put an end to exploitation, all national oppression and advance to a socialist world. Build the Communist League – Join our Campaign."

candidates.name: Helen Spiby-Vann
candidates.statement_to_voters:
We are the only party to lower taxes and recover taxes from multinationals to fund our policies. We are the only party to write policies which tackle the root causes of poverty.

We would raise £40.5bn on a 5% turnover tax on multinationals Amazon, Microsoft, Facebook, Starbucks, Shell etc, who send all their profits abroad to avoid paying Corporation Tax (it would be offset against Corporation Tax - so British companies would pay less).

We would stop public spending on ‘woke’ diversity schemes and partisan campaigns. Also remove some additional ‘social requirements’ for Government contracts which are costing £379bn2 per year, prioritising value for money. Slashing these by 10% would save about £37.9bn.

I'm married with 3 children. I co-founded a food bank in NW3 during lockdown which gave me oversight of vulnerable people and insight into their needs.

I've been involved with various out-reaches over the years including helping the homeless, supporting destitute women and refugees. I’ve campaigned on parental views being represented in school RSE. I’m a member of the SACRE committee in my area. I work part time as a designer. 
In terms of lawmaking, the closer we align our laws with those of the creator, the more holistic the result. Only God’s laws (not man made laws) judge the thoughts and attitudes of the heart to restrain wrongdoing.

candidates.name: Patrick Thomas Stillman
candidates.statement_to_voters:
"I'm proud to have been selected as the Liberal Democrat candidate for Holborn and St Pancras. Voters here deserve better than a Labour Government in chaos, or a Green Party using this seat to prop up its leader's ambitions.

“We have a distinct, confident liberal message - on housing, on safety, on giving young Londoners like me a fair shot at building a life here - and I'm going to make that case on every doorstep between now and October 8th.”

candidates.name: Lauren Bird
candidates.statement_to_voters:
Lauren has been living in Rosemount for over five years now. Working in public facing roles in and around the city she’s got to know the city and the people living here well. She has always cared deeply for people and communities as well as nature and the environment. She wants Aberdeen to thrive and live up to its potential.

If you want someone who truly cares for the people living here and our environment vote for the Scottish Greens October 8th.

candidates.name: Simon McLean
candidates.statement_to_voters:
Simon is keen to put Aberdeen first and is concerned with the current debt to the London Stock Exchange owed by Aberdeen City Council.  He would like to protect all local services.  He was a volunteer on his local community council and held the position of voluntary Chair of Planning and Transport for the Aberdeen community council forum.
Simon has seen and experienced how communities are treated by elements within the council and seeks to improve the local government.
He would also like to take pressure off mental health and GP surgery services.  He is happy to be contacted on any issue of concern to local residents.

candidates.name: Andrew Fox-Hewitt
candidates.statement_to_voters:
I have lived in Newcastle for 40 years, went to school at Hassell Street in Town, worked at the local fire station, and have previously been a councillor.

My wife works at our hospital and my children go to school here.

I have spent my entire adult life in public service.

Our town centre is declining, and our council is dysfunctional under the Reform administration, so I've decided to put myself forward for residents to have an alternative to the chaos and decline, someone who will fight to protect our green spaces and environment, and for people of all ages to feel safe in our wonderful town.

candidates.name: Anya Krycek
candidates.party_name_on_ballot: The Socialist Party of Great Britain
candidates.statement_to_voters: Anya Krycek is an Irish-born radical feminist and socialist theoretician who has lived in South London for 21 years, bringing together deep expertise in feminist studies with committed revolutionary politics as a member of the Socialist Party of Great Britain. A regular contributor to The Socialist Standard  she synthesizes radical feminist analysis with impossiblism and orthodox Marxist theory to examine the interconnected systems of patriarchy and capitalism, rejecting reformist approaches in favour of fundamental social transformation. Her political work is grounded in practical community engagement, including hands-on animal rescue volunteering that aligns with her ethical framework a life long strict vegetarian, and she is currently putting these principles into electoral practice as the SPGB candidate for Brixton North in the May 2026 local elections and now candidate for Lambeth July 9th election for Clapham Park, where her two decades of embedded local knowledge inform her advocacy for the ward's residents

candidates.name: Sonia Winifred
candidates.statement_to_voters:
Everyone should have the right to live in a decent home, breathe clean air, and ensure a safer, greener planet for the next generation to enjoy. We need to invest in our communities and create an economy where all voices are listened to. We need change and hope for the future!

But after twenty years as a member of the Labour Party, and ten years as councillor and Lambeth cabinet member for the Equalities and Culture portfolio, I saw communities like mine become invisible to the Labour Party. Our voices weren’t heard.

Thousands of residents petitioned Lambeth Council to vote for a motion calling for a ceasefire in Gaza – but when I refused to vote against the Gaza ceasefire motion that the Greens brought, Labour suspended me.

Lambeth residents deserve better, and they have been ignored for far too long! I joined the Green Party to change that, and since May they’ve begun to change that in Lambeth by listening and inviting the community to have a say in how services are delivered.

I am totally committed to representing the residents of Myatt’s Fields and the challenge of fixing Lambeth’s broken housing and repair systems, empowering our communities, and fighting for people every day.

candidates.name: John Bloxsom
candidates.statement_to_voters:
John is committed to being a accountable and accessible councillor who reports back to you. John will strive to make our communities better, greener and more sustainable - great places to live and work. John pledges:
* to work with you and support our communities to make a difference at Shire Hall
* to challenge the years of Conservative neglect, from children's services to roads 
* to support public transport, cycle routes and sustainable investment to respond to the climate emergency

candidates.name: Robin Layfield
candidates.statement_to_voters:
I have been a Parish Councillor for Rodborough since 2018 and I was a District Councillor for the Ward from 2021 — 2024.

I have lived and worked in Rodborough for the best part of my life and I can often been seen around the Parish. Stop me and say hi, I'm always available for a chat.

I am a member of the Stroud District Green Party, where I serve as the Trade Union Liaison Officer (TULO). I am a member of Unite Community and the Communication Workers Union (United Tech and Allied Workers). I have and will always stand up for the rights of workers.

I have worked with charity fundraisers, Stroud District Foodbank, Rodborough Sunday Social, Rodborough Youth and Rodborough CAN (Climate Action Network), to help meet the needs of our most vulnerable, young and elderly residents and to begin the work of building a sustainable and resilient community in Rodborough.

Right now, with so much uncertainty around Local Government Reorganisation, Rodborough needs someone who can step in and hit the ground running. I am that person - I have years of District Council experience at the most senior levels, I understand what the council is going through and I am determined to give the community a stronger voice in local government.

My council roles have included:

* Alliance Leadership Team * Vice Chair Environment Committee * Equality, Diversity & Inclusion Member Champion * Equality, Diversity, Inclusion & Equity Working Group * Chair, Members Development Working Group * Board Director, Stroud Valleys Canal Company * SDC Regeneration Board * 2030 Community Engagement Board * Stroud Town Council Regeneration Committee

I work as a web developer for agencies across the country. In my spare time I write for the Rodborough Commoner, Amplify Stroud and Good on Paper. I am an event organiser and host with For Your Information and have received 3 awards for community leadership.

I am fiercely committed to honesty, representation, advocacy and being a clear voice for our community.

“I am putting myself forward to represent Rodborough on the District Council so that I can play my part in achieving our climate goals for 2030. The Climate and Nature Emergency is the biggest threat to us all now and in the future.”

candidates.name: Kristina Renshaw
candidates.statement_to_voters:
I am standing as a candidate because I believe our communities deserve honest representation, common sense policies, and a voice that truly reflects the will of local people.

My values align strongly with those of the Heritage Party: protecting our cultural heritage, supporting families and communities, protecting our children, defending free speech, restoring democratic accountability, and putting the interests of the Welsh people first.

If elected, I will work to:

• Defend local democracy and transparency
• Protect our communities and public services
• Oppose inappropriate developments such as HMOs that damage neighbourhoods
• Stand up for common sense, fairness, and accountability in local government
• Ensure residents’ voices are heard and respected
• Oppose Nation of Sanctuary

This campaign is not about political games. It is about restoring trust in local politics and giving residents a representative who will listen, speak honestly, and stand firm for what is right.

If you believe in common sense, community, and democracy, I would be honoured to have your support.

Together we can put residents first again.

candidates.name: Josh Swash
candidates.party_description_on_ballot: Flintshire People's Voice Candidate | Ymgeisydd Llais Pobl Sir y Fflint
candidates.statement_to_voters:
I'm Josh, and I'm standing in the by-election on the 15th October to represent our village on Flintshire County Council. I will always put the interests of Higher Kinnerton first. This is my home too.

I have lived in Higher Kinnerton for seven years, and it's a place I'm proud to call home. It's a fantastic village with a strong community spirit, but we need to make sure we have a strong voice representing us at County Hall - someone who will stand up for residents and make sure our village gets the attention it deserves.

I'm committed to our community. I am trustee of the village hall, and I serve on the community council, a voluntary role, where I have never been afraid to speak up for residents or question decisions when I believe they are not in the best interests of our community. In my day job, I work in our NHS.

I believe Higher Kinnerton needs a committed local voice to fight for our community. That means fixing the potholes in and around the village, fighting proposals for inappropriate development on green spaces, and improving our bus service, with evening and Sunday services. It means producing a community speed plan to make our village safer for children and older people, and sorting the drainage issues which leave parts of the village vulnerable to flooding. It means opposing continued council tax hikes, as I have done consistently on the community council, by targeting genuine waste.

candidates.name: Oliver Martin Wilson
candidates.party_description_on_ballot: Welsh Conservative Party Candidate | Ymgeisydd Plaid Geidwadol Cymru

candidates.name: Katy Brookes-Duncan
candidates.statement_to_voters: I am committed to fighting for a fairer funding deal for Leicestershire and in particular Shepshed. I will be an accountable representative for the community in Shepshed and will garner their views in order to inform my work as a County Councillor. My priorities are to ensure the Council support economic recovery, delivering the basics better (including social care) and cutting waste, safer roads and safer, cleaner and greener communities.

candidates.name: Piers Martin Kotting
candidates.statement_to_voters: Having seen how local services are falling short for young people and families, both first-hand and when setting up a social enterprise to assist families during the pandemic, I’m standing for election to fight for better support and accountability, and to improve services for all families. As a small business owner, I also understand the pressures facing local businesses and the frustrations of red tape and rising costs. Although I haven’t held elected office before, I bring extensive experience from roles in the NHS and private sector, which I am committed to using to make a real difference for our community.

candidates.name: Laura Elizabeth Jones
candidates.statement_to_voters:
I’m delighted to have been selected as the Conservative candidate for the upcoming Milford by-election.

As a local mum, I care deeply about our area and want to see it flourish. Over the past four years, I have served as Fundraising Officer for the Milford Area Preservation Group, helping to protect and preserve this historic place.

candidates.name: Mac McIntyre Brown
candidates.statement_to_voters:
Mac works as a social and healthcare management specialist, and he is dedicated to improving the life experience of residents and their families in Salisbury.

As a Salisbury City Councillor, he already understands the challenges many in our community face.

Mac says: “I want to see justice for Salisbury which to me means as many decisions as possible about Salisbury being made here in Salisbury and a fairer deal on issues like the price of car parking.”

As an active member of the planning committee, Mac has been closely involved in protecting the city’s social and physical infrastructure from the pressures of over‑development.

This by-election will be close between hard-working Lib Dems and chaos and decline with the Conservatives and Reform UK. 
Our Priorities for Milford

1. SAFER ROADS. Too many roads in Milford are used as 'rat runs', with residents experiencing speeding, congestion and damage to cars. Mac and Lawrence will push Wiltshire Council to work with residents to find creative solutions to the problems in streets such as Rampart Road, Milford Mill Road, Wain-A-Long Road and the surrounding areas. 
     
2. ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR. Mac and Lawrence will work to ensure that residents' voices are heard and that there is a joined-up approach to tackling anti-social behaviour involving the police, both councils and social housing providers. They will also champion positive solutions such as rebuilding our youth services.
     
3. AFFORDABLE HOUSING. Mac will work with the Lib Dems to ensure residents' voices are heard during the development of the new local plan. Any expansion of housing must ensure local needs for affordable housing are met and environmental concerns are taken into account.

candidates.name: Daisy Gilpin
candidates.statement_to_voters:
I’m delighted to have been selected as the Green Party candidate for Calverley and Farsley.

I live in Rodley, have an allotment in Calverley, and spend a lot of time in our green spaces and supporting local businesses. I care deeply about our area and the people who call it home. I’m excited to get out into our communities, listen to residents and ask: “What can I do to help?”

I joined the Green Party because, for the first time in a long time, I felt hopeful about what a different kind of politics could look like. I’m incredibly proud to have the opportunity to contribute, and I can’t wait to get started.

candidates.name: Kathryn Sara Penny
candidates.statement_to_voters:
I’ve loved living in our community for 11 years and I want to help make it a place where everyone can flourish just as my family and I have. I’m honoured to be a candidate in the local elections in May and it’s been a privilege to speak to so many residents about what matters to them during my campaign.

I’m passionate about road safety, protecting and investing in our green spaces and supporting residents who may be struggling with the cost of living. As a mum and an educator I also care deeply about developing spaces where young people can play, create and build skills.

If elected as your councillor my priorities will be

**Protecting and investing in green spaces** – safeguarding our parks, paths, canal and green belt for future generations.

**Improving road safety** – making our roads safer for pedestrians, cyclists and drivers.

**Creating opportunities for young people** – expanding opportunities and support to give every young person the best possible start in life.

**Supporting residents with cost of living** – standing up for families and pensioners facing rising bills and financial pressure and fighting for investment in public services such as libraries, clean streets and improved transport links.

I really love our community and I want to make it a great place to grow up, work and live. I am not a career politician and I can bring my experience of leadership in my other jobs to represent you with focus and professionalism.

**I want to be your councillor because I have a passion for making the place we call home even better, across all our areas of Calverley, Farsley, Pudsey, Rodley, Stanningley, Thornbury and Woodhall. I’d be grateful for your support.**

candidates.name: Dan Clarke
candidates.statement_to_voters:
I’m Dan Clarke, I’m the Libertarian Party Parliamentary candidate for the Makerfield by-election. Which is taking place on 18th June. I am also standing in a local council by election for Farnworth ward (Widnes) which is taking place on 25th June.

Our main principles are lower taxes, maximum personal freedom and implementation of a Constitution for the United Kingdom. We want to Enshrine the right to digital freedoms into constitutional law. We are completely against the “Digital ID” that this authoritarian government is obsessed in pushing through.

The big issues I see in Makerfield are huge dislike of Keir Starmer. This is definitely a by-election to get rid of Starmer, regardless of who wins. If I win, I will champion constituents right to privacy. I will work tirelessly to stop ‘Digital ID’ From happening. People have a right to privacy.

The time for classical liberalism/Libertarianism is now. The movement is growing, we are fighting more elections. We are showing the UK that we are here, we are serious and we will eventually succeed.
